items.stem: Which sentence correctly matches its verb to both the subject and the time?

options.text: The list of applicant were posted on the board yesterday.
The list of applicants were posted on the board yesterday.
The list of applicants was posted on the board yesterday.
The list of applicants is posted on the board yesterday.

reveal.terms: Error recognition: find the sentence with no error in agreement, tense, pronoun, preposition or word form.
reveal.shortcut: Check the subject-verb pair first, then tense words, then pronouns and prepositions.
reveal.why_correct: The subject is "list" (singular), so the verb is "was"; "yesterday" needs past tense.

why_wrong.o2: "were" agrees with "applicants", the nearest noun, not the subject "list".
why_wrong.o4: "is" is present tense, but "yesterday" needs the past.
why_wrong.o1: "applicant" must be plural after "list of", and "were" still mismatches "list".

options.text: The office will release its report since Monday.
The office will released its report on Monday.
The office will release it's report on Monday.
The office will release its report on Monday.

reveal.terms: Error recognition: find the sentence with no error in agreement, tense, pronoun, preposition or word form.
reveal.shortcut: Check the subject-verb pair first, then tense words, then pronouns and prepositions.
reveal.why_correct: "its" is the possessive; "will" takes the base verb; "on Monday" names a day.

why_wrong.o1: "since" needs a past starting point and a perfect tense, not a future plan.

items.stem: Which sentence uses the correct pronoun after a preposition?

options.text: Between you and me, the memo is unclear.
Between you and myself, the memo is unclear.
Between you and I, the memo is unclear.
Among you and me, the memo is unclear.

reveal.terms: Error recognition: find the sentence with no error in agreement, tense, pronoun, preposition or word form.
reveal.shortcut: Check the subject-verb pair first, then tense words, then pronouns and prepositions.
reveal.why_correct: After a preposition ("between"), use the object pronoun "me".

why_wrong.o3: "I" is a subject pronoun; a preposition needs "me".
why_wrong.o4: "Among" is for three or more; two people take "between".
why_wrong.o2: "myself" is reflexive and needs "I" earlier in the sentence.

items.stem: Which sentence uses verb tenses correctly?

options.text: When the auditor arrived, the clerk had already filed the vouchers.
When the auditor arrived, the clerk has already filed the vouchers.
When the auditor arrived, the clerk had already file the vouchers.
When the auditor arrives, the clerk had already filed the vouchers.

reveal.terms: Error recognition: find the sentence with no error in agreement, tense, pronoun, preposition or word form.
reveal.shortcut: Check the subject-verb pair first, then tense words, then pronouns and prepositions.
reveal.why_correct: The earlier past action (filing) takes the past perfect "had filed" beside the simple past "arrived".

why_wrong.o2: "has filed" (present perfect) clashes with the past "arrived".

items.stem:
Using standard alphabetic filing for business names, which name is filed FIRST?
The Bayanihan Store | Carino Bakery | Dagupan Hardware | Ermita Printing

options.text: Ermita Printing
Carino Bakery
The Bayanihan Store
Dagupan Hardware

reveal.terms: Index each business name into units ("The" last, symbols spelled out, digits first), then compare unit by unit.
reveal.why_correct: "The" as the first word becomes the last unit: Bayanihan Store The, which files under B, first. This follows the standard office filing rule (ARMA International Simplified Filing Standard Rules, Rule 2), not a rule published by the CSC. Source standard: ANSI/ARMA 12-2005.

why_wrong.o2: Files first only if "The" is counted as the first unit (T).
why_wrong.o4: D comes after B and C.
why_wrong.o1: E comes after B, C and D.

items.source: Civio Filing Rules v2 / ARMA Rule 2
items.reviewer: Chief of Staff (final approval, delegated by GT)

items.stem:
Using standard alphabetic filing for business names, which name is filed FIRST?
21st Century Printing | 5 Star Bakery | Ace Trading | Five Brothers Hardware

options.text: 21st Century Printing
Five Brothers Hardware
Ace Trading
5 Star Bakery

reveal.terms: Index each business name into units ("The" last, symbols spelled out, digits first), then compare unit by unit.
reveal.why_correct: Digits file before letters in ascending order, so 5 comes before 21 (ordinal "st" ignored). This follows the standard office filing rule (ARMA International Simplified Filing Standard Rules, Rule 7), not a rule published by the CSC. Source standard: ANSI/ARMA 12-2005.

why_wrong.o1: Numerically 21 is greater than 5. Comparing the digits as text ("2" before "5") would wrongly put it first.
why_wrong.o3: Names that begin with letters file after names that begin with digits.
why_wrong.o2: A spelled-out number files alphabetically under F.

items.source: Civio Filing Rules v2 / ARMA Rule 7
items.reviewer: Chief of Staff (final approval, delegated by GT)

items.stem:
Using standard alphabetic filing for business names, which name is filed LAST?
Tan-Go Grocery | Tan Lee Bakery | Tanauan Hardware | Tang Printing

options.text: Tan Lee Bakery
Tan-Go Grocery
Tanauan Hardware
Tang Printing

reveal.terms: Index each business name into units ("The" last, symbols spelled out, digits first), then compare unit by unit.
reveal.why_correct: A hyphenated name is one unit: TanGo. Order: Tan Lee (Tan alone, nothing before something), Tanauan, Tang, TanGo. TanGo is last. This follows the standard office filing rule (ARMA International Simplified Filing Standard Rules, Rule 3), not a rule published by the CSC. Source standard: ANSI/ARMA 12-2005.

why_wrong.o1: "Tan" as a short first unit files first, not last.
why_wrong.o4: Last only if Tan-Go is split into two units (Tan, Go), which puts it at the front.

items.source: Civio Filing Rules v2 / ARMA Rule 3
